rv.q: Handbagged promises much and delivers very little. It's vaguely interesting and occasionally genuinely involving, particularly when Mohan and Woolgar are in the spotlight.
But sadly it just continues as more of the same, and there is no real play to speak of at all.
This is one of the many reasons why this play deserves a sell-out audience, and by the looks of things, it is starting to happen, so book while you still can!

Whilst the show is incredibly funny, and in itself a history lesson for those of us not old enough to remember Thatcher’s premiership, it has great heart and wit, and never fails to entertain, move and enlighten its audience.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this dual-cast portrayal of Queen Elizabeth and Margaret Thatcher. While some praise its clever premise and humor, others find the device grows tiresome, with the concept wearing thin by the second half.
